The guard lives in **`pkg/okf/provenance.go`**, in the function **`ensureNoForgedHumanVerification(fullPath string, c *Concept, actor string, isNew bool) error`**. It returns early (allows everything) when the actor is a human — determined by **`IsHumanIdentity`** in the same file — and otherwise rejects the save if the concept carries any human verification (`IsHumanIdentity(v.By)`) that is not already recorded on disk. The set of pre-existing verifications it's allowed to preserve comes from **`recordedVerifications`** (also in `provenance.go`), which reads and parses the concept file already at `fullPath`; a new concept (`isNew`) inherits nothing. When a non-human actor like the MCP server agent tries to add a fresh `verified.by: human...` entry, it fails with `actor %q cannot add human verification %q`.

This guard is invoked during the save path from **`saveConceptLocked`** in **`pkg/okf/mutate.go`** (call at line 494), which passes the self-declared `actor` and `opts.IsNew`. Because the actor is self-declared, the check specifically protects callers that cannot forge a human identity (the MCP server) rather than authenticating a CLI `--actor`.
